ibd-9176ef1c6ad9ca7c-q12:whole.hint: Consider the system and its surroundings together. A local entropy decrease need not violate the second law.

ibd-bda1b131f5bd7daf-q7:whole.hint: Work is connected to the change in volume. On a pressure–volume graph, look for the relevant area.

ibd-0eb4c5443f7ce547-qB3:2.a.hint: Translate “isothermal” into a statement about temperature, then consider what that means for an ideal gas’s internal energy.
notes: For an ideal gas in an isothermal process, ΔU = 0 and therefore Q = W using work done by the gas. A fixed amount obeys pV = constant.
No temperature change does not mean no heat transfer. Heat can enter during expansion to replace the energy transferred out as work.

ibd-0eb4c5443f7ce547-qB3:2.b.hint: Translate “isothermal” into a statement about temperature, then consider what that means for an ideal gas’s internal energy.

ibd-0eb4c5443f7ce547-qB3:2.c.hint: Which energy-transfer route is excluded by “adiabatic”? Apply the first law with that term removed.
notes: Adiabatic means Q = 0, so ΔU = −W when W is work done by the gas. Expansion can cool the gas; compression can warm it.
For a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas process, pV^γ is constant (γ = C_p/C_v). Do not replace this with pV = constant, which belongs to an isothermal process.
Link the relevant physical cause to the observation asked about. Naming a law alone does not explain why this particular result follows.

ibd-8613550f6b9feda1-q8:whole.hint: Treat the gas as the system and mark the directions of heat and work before substituting numbers.
notes: With W positive for work done by the gas and Q positive into it, ΔU = Q − W. “Rejects heat” makes Q negative; compression makes W negative.
For an ideal gas, internal energy depends on temperature. An unchanged temperature does not by itself mean no heat or work transfer.

ibd-8613550f6b9feda1-q9:whole.hint: Draw the energy entering from the hot reservoir, the useful work and the energy rejected to the cold reservoir.
notes: Over a complete engine cycle ΔU = 0, so W = Q_hot − Q_cold and efficiency = W/Q_hot. Use energy per cycle or power consistently.
Only an ideal reversible Carnot engine reaches η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot. Both reservoir temperatures must be in kelvin; this gives an upper bound for a real engine.

ibd-a23732ed0006f612-q11:whole.hint: If the volume cannot change, which term in the first law disappears?

notes: Adiabatic means Q = 0, so ΔU = −W when W is work done by the gas. Expansion can cool the gas; compression can warm it.
For a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas process, pV^γ is constant (γ = C_p/C_v). Do not replace this with pV = constant, which belongs to an isothermal process.

The enclosed area of a complete cycle is net work, with its sign set by the direction around the cycle. Convert kPa, MPa, litres and any axis multipliers before calculating.

fep-2e1fc42dcfce27b2-qA3:a.text: Entropy measures the number of microscopic arrangements compatible with a macroscopic state. Greater spreading of energy among available states corresponds to greater entropy; “greater disorder” is a qualitative description of this.

fep-2e1fc42dcfce27b2-qA3:b.text: The total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. Equivalently, ΔSsystem + ΔSsurroundings ≥ 0: it is zero for an ideal reversible process and positive for an irreversible process.

fep-2e1fc42dcfce27b2-qA3:c.text: The egg is not an isolated system. Its local increase in organization is accompanied by transfers of energy and matter to its surroundings. The increase in the surroundings’ entropy compensates for any decrease in the egg’s entropy, so the total entropy does not decrease.

fep-66ce32ec6c971df5-qB4:1.d.text: Entropy measures the number of microscopic arrangements compatible with a macroscopic state. Greater spreading of energy among available states corresponds to greater entropy; “greater disorder” is a qualitative description of this.

fep-66ce32ec6c971df5-qB4:1.e.text: The total entropy of an isolated system cannot decrease. Equivalently, ΔSsystem + ΔSsurroundings ≥ 0: it is zero for an ideal reversible process and positive for an irreversible process.

fep-66ce32ec6c971df5-qB4:1.f.text: The water’s entropy decreases as it becomes a more ordered solid. Freezing releases latent heat into the surroundings, increasing their entropy. The total entropy change is non-negative: zero in the ideal reversible limit, and positive in an actual irreversible process.
